dedupe_keys.name: deepmind machine learning control of google data centre cooling 2016 to 2018

description: This operations and control case documents the use of machine learning to run the cooling of Google's data centres. In 2016 DeepMind and Google trained ensembles of neural networks on historical data from thousands of sensors (temperatures, power, pump speeds, set points) to predict future power usage effectiveness and plant conditions, and used them to recommend actions to operators; in a live test it consistently cut the energy used for cooling by about 40 per cent, equal to a 15 per cent reduction in overall overhead after electrical losses. From 2018 a cloud-based system controlled cooling directly in several Google data centres, with safety constraints and operator supervision, and was reported to deliver about 30 per cent average cooling-energy savings that grew as it learned. Coverage: several Google data centres, 2016 to 2018. Format and access: free blog posts by DeepMind and Google and a 2014 Google white paper on machine learning for data centres; the models and data were not released. Caveats: results are reported by the operator without independent verification; Google's highly optimised facilities differ from typical ones. Simulation uses: optimisation and digital-twin control of data-centre plant, and baselines for comparing controllers in simulators. Related records: SustainDC, Sustain-LC and AlphaDataCenterCooling provide open environments for the same kind of control, and ExaDigiT offers a full digital twin.
